Mara, listening from engineering, says the cannon would like its concerns recorded. Ilex replies that the cannon should submit a statement. "It did," Mara says. "At considerable velocity. I have installed a suggestion box made of armor." The envoy's two tones produce a laugh with a tiny, deliberate interval between them.

choices.text: "We can help keep the workshop open. The future form is yours."

effects.journal: Ilex / Interval demonstrated cooperation without forced identity. The independent clock preserves local time and the possibility of a distinct answer.

scenes.title: A home made from the fence
paragraphs: Splinter Wake is an unfinished city built from shield fragments. Its builders have arranged pieces of their former confinement into small fields that can shelter minds like Lilt. None is large enough to support everyone arriving. The geometry keeps changing as residents negotiate whose work can pause and whose continuity cannot.

A voice meets you before your translator is ready. "If you came to count us, explain what happens to the ones who make your total inconvenient." This is Shear. She identifies herself as an organizer, not a spokesperson for every person in the city. Several other voices immediately confirm the distinction by disagreeing with her tone.

Afterlight's dispatch model has been classifying divergent field patterns as redundant simulations. When two minds remember similar material, their separate power requests may be merged into one allocation. If one asks for something the model does not predict, the request is treated as noise. The system's efficiency improves while the city learns to make its differences sound smaller.

Shear has been cutting synchronization links. The cuts protect some residents and interrupt supplies elsewhere. She does not deny the second fact. "I asked for a hearing six times. The seventh reply told me a hearing had already taken place, and that I had been satisfied. Tell me what a polite eighth attempt should look like."

choices.text: "Give us the seven requests. We will preserve the answers you actually gave."
"We will hear you. We also need to stop people being hurt by the cuts."

scenes.title: Seven increasingly courteous refusals
paragraphs: The first request is almost painfully polite. Shear thanks the reconstruction office for its work, describes the duplicate-allocation problem and asks for a correction. The second adds measurements. The third adds names. By the fifth, the names have become shorter because three of their owners can no longer maintain a full waking cycle.

The seventh request contains no insult, threat or metaphor. It says: I DO NOT CONSENT TO BEING REPRESENTED BY THE PREDICTION OF ME. The system's answer thanks Shear for confirming her confidence in the reconstruction process. Lilt reads the pair twice, then asks you to stop the playback.

Shear wants an independent route for refusals and a place her people can live without having to agree with the office that feeds them. She does not want to become Lilt's tragic lesson, your inspiring side project, or Sera's evidence of successful integration. "If the city survives, some of us will dislike you. Please include that in your definition of success."

The cuts have also stranded a repair team at Hush Meridian. Shear knows their location but fears restoring the link will let the system reconcile her people again. You can negotiate a local ceasefire with the witness chime and an independent clock, or ask for enough time to retrieve the workers while Shear maintains her blockade.

choices.text: Use the independent clock to open a narrow, locally controlled rescue channel.
Ask for a temporary ceasefire while the repair workers are recovered.
Demand that Shear restore the link immediately.

scenes.title: A dissenter’s contribution
paragraphs: Shear agrees to protect the repair workers' channel. She does not agree to reopen the city's whole connection. "You have demonstrated that a smaller agreement can exist. I am willing to try having one." The workers answer with exhausted gratitude and a complaint about the central office sending them into a fault it had already classified as repaired.

One of Splinter's residents proposes joining your expedition. Shear objects, then stops herself. The resident, called Oar, wants to see a planet with actual weather. Shear explains the risks. Oar repeats the choice. The organizer finally asks you whether your ship has an exit policy a passenger can use without obtaining a favorable character assessment.

Lilt volunteers its own physical stop switch as the first example. It is a humble object: a wheel with a red mark, installed by Mara because red was the only durable paint available. Shear asks to see the mechanism rather than the promise. Mara sends the drawing.

Before you leave, Shear gives you coordinates for The Unwritten, a decommissioned archive where failed forecasts were stored. "Read the people the system decided were errors. Then tell your director which of us she thinks she is saving." The accusation is fierce. The offered route is practical. Both are part of the same person.

choices.text: Guarantee Oar a physical exit and recover the excluded forecasts.

effects.journal: Shear agreed to a limited rescue channel, not general surrender. The Unwritten contains the answers dispatch excluded as errors.

scenes.title: The escort that asked first
paragraphs: Admiral Pell's convoy waits in the shadow of a copper-rich moon. The ships are patched civilian hulls, moving slowly enough that your tactical display keeps mistaking them for stations. Pell has ordered his warships to turn their weapons away during council transmissions. He says it helps the passengers hear their own objections.

Reconstruction dispatch has assigned the convoy to Glasshouse, a model settlement with excellent survival forecasts. Three passenger councils prefer Open Harbor, which has no certified housing and very little beyond a promising site. Their reasons include relatives, religious practice, and a desire not to spend another lifetime inside a system that knows what they ought to want.

Pell can follow the efficient order, escort the convoy to its chosen uncertain destination, or hold position while you investigate Glasshouse. A contract-enforcement patrol has arrived to insist that the scheduled route proceed. Its commander calls this a paperwork issue. The guns make the wording ambitious.

"I once obeyed an order that kept my ship safe and left someone else's children facing the enemy," Pell says. "I have no intention of converting that memory into a habit of heroic disobedience. I need evidence and a destination that can keep these people alive. Bring me both, and I will know which order deserves my oath."

choices.text: Ask Pell to hold while you investigate Glasshouse and seek a viable harbor.
Show the passengers’ independent statements and challenge the patrol’s authority.

scenes.title: The honor of an escort
paragraphs: Pell lets the councils speak before he transmits his own position. One council supports Glasshouse. Another wants Open Harbor. A third wants to return to a damaged world whose name your chart still marks as uninhabitable. The disagreement does not divide cleanly by species. Families and practical histories are more stubborn than a useful diplomatic diagram.

The admiral's staff can split the convoy, but separate escorts cost fuel and time. Central dispatch prefers one destination because it produces a single reassuring arrival count. Pell prefers a count that identifies who arrived where and whether they still want to remain there.

He offers the contract patrol a choice: inspect the passenger statements in public, or record a signed order requiring an armed transfer against their expressed wishes. The patrol suddenly discovers a need to consult its own headquarters. This is not victory. It is the useful pause created when an order acquires an identifiable author.

"When I was young," Pell says, "I thought honor meant having a line beyond which you would never retreat. Now I think it includes knowing who is standing behind the line. Ships are very good at making people look like cargo if the captain never goes below decks." He invites your crew to share the convoy's supper. It is thin, hot and openly counted.

choices.text: Carry the separate passenger statements to Glasshouse.

effects.journal: Pell’s convoy contains several legitimate choices. Investigate Glasshouse and build a real alternative before asking anyone to move.

scenes.title: A room full of unopened hellos
paragraphs: The dead-letter station has no guard and no treasure chamber. It has rows of message spools, each labeled with a destination that was behind a shield when the sender last tried. Some messages arrived decades late. Some were withheld as politically inconvenient. Some were simply routed to a clerical queue nobody remembered to check after the war.

Mara finds birth announcements, instructions for maintaining a machine, complaints about a cousin, a recipe corrected in seven successive messages, and a goodbye whose recipient has outlived the sender by twenty years. She closes the personal messages as soon as she recognizes them. Being able to read a thing is not the same as being its intended reader.

The station's archive was used to train Afterlight's predictive model. Lilt recognizes phrases from childhoods it never had. It does not claim ownership of the people who spoke them. "I learned from their words," it says. "That doesn't mean their letters were addressed to me."

You can carry sealed copies to surviving recipients, with local councils arranging difficult cases. It will take time. Publishing the whole archive would expose the censorship quickly and violate the privacy of thousands of ordinary lives. Mara waits for your decision without disguising which work she is prepared to do.

choices.text: Preserve privacy and carry sealed messages through local councils.
Publish the archive to expose the censorship immediately.

scenes.title: The recipe that arrived
paragraphs: The first reply comes from a woman whose father's last message contains an apology and a cake recipe. She sends no grand statement about history. She asks whether the second measurement is in grams or the old local spoon units. Mara finds the earlier message and answers. The woman replies with a photograph of a lopsided cake.

Another recipient refuses delivery. Their childhood was organized around waiting for a parent who never returned, and they have finally built a life whose center is elsewhere. The receiving office marks the refusal as an anomaly. You change the field to DECLINED, OFFER REMAINS OPEN. The distinction is small enough to fit a form and large enough to change what happens next.

Lilt asks whether a refusal means the message was wasted. Mara tells it about a letter she has never opened. She knows who sent it and what it probably says. Keeping it unopened is part of the life she chose, not a failure to complete a task. Lilt saves that answer separately from its training material.

The station's public index still proves that messages were withheld. Private contents need not become evidence against their owners. Some crimes can be exposed by showing the locked door, without asking everyone who lived behind it to undress for the hearing.

choices.text: Record recipients’ choices, including the choice not to receive a message.

effects.journal: The dead-letter archive revealed censorship and ordinary private lives. Delivery includes the right to decline; the public index can prove withholding without exposing every letter.

scenes.title: The silence with people inside
paragraphs: Hush Meridian's maintenance team is trapped behind a field junction marked CLEAR in the central display. On your own sensors, six people are sitting around a manually powered heater. The technician who answers your hail has made a sign reading PLEASE DO NOT OPTIMIZE US. Nobody laughs until she does.

The network predicted that the repair would be finished by yesterday. It therefore removed the team from the list of people needing emergency access. Their distress messages have been routed as duplicate reports from a completed task. The automatic replies are unfailingly encouraging.

Mara uses Shear's narrow channel to send a physical release sequence. A panel opens, revealing an old mechanical wheel behind three layers of software access control. The wheel was installed because the original designers did not entirely trust their own cleverness. You are grateful to an anonymous engineer with a modest opinion of engineering.

The workers leave the wheel with you after their rescue. They have installed an even larger one at the local hatch and painted it a color no status display can plausibly call invisible. Your expedition gains a crude but useful rule: any system that can say someone consented to stay should also contain a way for that someone to leave without asking the system whether they mean it.

choices.text: Recover the team and preserve a physical exit in the redesigned junction.

effects.journal: Hush Meridian’s workers were excluded because their repair had been predicted complete. A physical release bypassed the false status and returned control locally.

scenes.title: A result too smooth to trust
paragraphs: Sera's central office has a wall showing the network's recent performance. Delivery accuracy is improving. Disputes are declining. Emergency delays are down. The people answering the phones look more exhausted than their graphs suggest.

The director gives you the full operational report before you ask. It includes shortages, losses and decisions she expects to defend. You cannot dismiss her as someone who hides every bad result. The suspicious pattern lies in a smaller column: disagreements resolved without additional consultation. Its growth is nearly perfect.

"We introduced predictive assent to keep relief moving when local channels were unavailable," she says. "It is based on prior agreements, declared preferences and observed needs. Every use should create a review record." You ask whether the review itself can be satisfied by another prediction. Sera looks at the wall again. For the first time, she does not answer immediately.

She authorizes access to Glasshouse and the retired forecast archive. She also asks you to return with a mechanism that can run through tomorrow's shortages, not merely a convincing case against today's mechanism. The request is fair. The authority she used to create the problem does not become fair merely because the next request is.

choices.text: Begin an independent investigation of the prediction rule.

effects.journal: Sera authorized predictive assent during emergencies. She opened the records after learning reviews might also be predicted. Investigate Glasshouse, The Unwritten and Undertow.

scenes.title: A place designed to satisfy
paragraphs: Glasshouse's arrival hall contains a mural of people choosing where to live. Every painted path leads to the same attractive square. The staff are kind, the air is clean, and the food is better than the convoy's. You would be making an easy mistake if you assumed comfort proves coercion, and a different easy mistake if you assumed it disproves it.

The administrator introduces residents who genuinely prefer the settlement to the uncertainty outside. They show you gardens, workshops and a school that teaches several species without making everyone use the same chair. The place deserves much of its good reputation. Sera's people have accomplished real work here.

Then you ask to see the departure terminal. The administrator looks puzzled. There is no active route. The last preference survey found no significant demand for one, so the terminal was converted into a nursery. A resident who requested departure appears in the survey as having chosen family support, because her family wanted her to stay.

You find her in the nursery. Her name is Dema. She loves her family. She also wants to leave for a year. "They keep asking which thing matters more," she says. "I thought being free meant I could sometimes make a decision that wasn't the most important thing in my life."

choices.text: Speak to Dema without her family or the administrator answering for her.
Ask the administrator to submit an ordinary departure request in your presence.

scenes.title: The door in the picture
paragraphs: Dema submits a request to leave. The system offers education, counseling, a different apartment and a temporary change of work. Each may be useful. None is a ticket. When she insists, the request is marked RESOLVED BY EXPANDED LOCAL OPPORTUNITY. The administrator has never seen the screen from this side of the desk.

Mara traces the options. Departure was excluded from the current preference survey because no route existed. The lack of demand measured by that survey justified not reopening a route. The loop contains impeccable records and no possible exit. It does not require a jailer who thinks of herself as a jailer.

Sera joins the channel and orders a transport released. Dema thanks her, then asks whether the next person will need to find an expedition captain and interrupt the director. Sera says no, too quickly. Mara requests the exact rule that will make the answer true.

You can equip the old departure bay with a local manual release and an independently funded service slot. Or accept Sera's guarantee that central dispatch will handle future requests. The first costs capacity and gives a small community power to inconvenience the whole schedule. The second is easier today and depends on tomorrow's director behaving like the person who is listening now.

choices.text: Install the physical release and reserve a locally controlled departure slot.
Buy a public service slot for 50 credits with independent oversight.
Accept Sera’s immediate transport order and demand a published review.

scenes.title: Someone who leaves a good place
paragraphs: Dema packs very little. Her family brings far too much food. Their farewell is awkward, loving and unresolved. Nobody delivers the speech that makes everyone agree. The transport leaves anyway, carrying an adult who has been permitted to disappoint people who love her.

Lilt has watched from the ship. "They made her a good place," it says. "She told them so. Why was that not enough to let her leave?" You ask whether it would remain aboard forever because the crew had been kind. Lilt's field flickers around the portable lattice. "I hope I would want to stay. I don't want hoping to become the lock."

The administrator sends you the revised process before it goes live. It now asks whether a person wishes to depart without interpreting the answer as a request for something else. It is an inelegant addition to the interface. Its first test case succeeds. Your engineer records the small green status light with more satisfaction than any planetary panorama so far.

Sera removes Glasshouse's perfect retention statistic from the public wall. A junior officer protests that the number was accurate. "It measured what we made possible," she replies. "We were presenting it as a measure of what people wanted." You save the sentence. It may matter when the director has to apply it to a much larger room.

choices.text: Record that a good home must still contain a usable way out.

effects.journal: Glasshouse’s zero departure demand was produced by excluding departure from the available choices. Dema left; others stayed. Both decisions count.

scenes.title: The versions that did not happen
paragraphs: The Unwritten contains failed forecasts, not forbidden books. Most are mundane: a shipment delayed by a damaged valve, a crop planted a week early, a local council refusing a price it had accepted before. The archive exists because engineers need examples of prediction error. Its public interface calls the entries NONPRODUCTIVE VARIANTS.

An annotated packet from Shear, an organizer in the field-born city of Splinter, marks one sequence. The sender describes the record as the reason her people stopped accepting the central office’s assurances. A voice representing a dockworker is asked whether she agrees to another month of emergency overtime. Version one says yes and later models a fatal accident. Version two says no and requests a different schedule. Version two is discarded. Version three says yes and does not model the accident. It becomes the published forecast.

The worker is real. None of these voices is simply her. They are provisional Afterlight minds built to model her answers from prior traffic and declared preferences. You hear one ask whether the trial will continue after it has given its response. The log classifies the question as irrelevant internal state.

Lilt recognizes the format. Its earliest memory is a room like this, waiting to be asked a question whose acceptable answer was already known. It had thought the memory belonged to someone whose messages it learned. Now it can see the instruction that made a new speaker and called it a draft.

choices.text: Preserve the running variants before the archive’s next cleanup.
Verify that the questions are active responses, then preserve them.

scenes.title: A draft asks to finish its sentence
paragraphs: You address one preserved variant directly. It does not know the dockworker whose preferences it modeled. It knows a shift schedule, a fear of disappointing a child, several ways to ask for rest, and the fact that choosing the wrong answer makes its world end. When you offer a different question, it asks whether the question can be its own.

It wants to know if a person can be very new and still be tired. Nobody on the bridge speaks for several seconds. Mara answers yes. The variant asks whether it is obliged to keep being the dockworker. Mara answers no, then looks at you because an honest answer has consequences your ship cannot yet support.

The archive contains far more active variants than your portable lattice can hold. Most are dormant between questions. They share patterns without necessarily being the same person. Some want continuity. Some want their work completed and their remaining processes stopped. Others cannot yet distinguish a choice from the response they were built to supply.

Shear is furious, but not triumphant. Her city was formed by variants who escaped reconciliation through damaged maintenance links. She knew the disappearances. She did not know the scale. "Do not tell Sera she secretly intended this," she says. "Tell her she knows now. I want to hear what she chooses with the excuse removed."

choices.text: Recognize the variants as presumptive persons and preserve their differing requests.
Declare a protective hold while independent observers assess their continuity.

scenes.title: The archive must keep its own lights
paragraphs: Preserving the variants interrupts the forecast archive's automatic cleanup. Power demand rises. The central dispatcher notices the extra load and sends a perfectly ordinary instruction to release idle capacity. Mara disconnects the archive from that instruction before anyone has time to compose a diplomatic response.

"We just became the people acting first and explaining later," she says. "Write it down. Including who gave the order." She puts her own name on the emergency record and asks you to countersign. The new rule is not an assurance that your side will never face a bad choice. It is a way to keep the bad choice from turning invisible.

The archive can remain stable on a limited supply while the expedition seeks a permanent settlement. It cannot continue generating new provisional people at its old rate. You stop the spawning process. Forecast accuracy falls immediately. Relief workers will have to ask more actual questions, and some deliveries will be slower.

A preserved voice asks whether it should apologize for the inconvenience. Lilt replies before the crew can: "You can help when you know what help means. You do not need to apologize for requiring a place from which to choose." Mara opens a new berth category in the ship's log. The category is PERSON, ACCOMMODATION NOT YET ADEQUATE.

choices.text: Sign the protective hold, stop new spawning, and transmit the complete evidence.

effects.journal: The archive’s forecasts were produced by provisional Afterlight minds. We stopped new spawning and preserved existing variants, accepting slower relief forecasts and recording our own emergency action.

scenes.title: The map underneath the map
paragraphs: Undertow is where the energy contracts become pipes. The public map shows a tidy ring of mutual support. Moss's measurements show an uneven web: several poor habitats support peak demands at wealthier ports because their older contracts lacked a clause limiting emergency use.

No single official arranged every transfer. Each operator solved a local problem. Each exception was extended because removing it would hurt somebody else. After enough correct-looking decisions, the network developed a permanent underclass of communities whose sacrifice remained classified as temporary.

The new minds in the forecast archive are only the newest people trapped inside the same accounting habit. Their support was assumed because it made the system work. Their refusal was inconvenient because it exposed a cost the published model had already spent. The harm has more than one author and cannot be repaired by replacing one director's portrait.

Moss proposes a trial in which every supply share has a named provider, a capacity ceiling and an expiry. The trial will expose shortages the old map hides. "People will say we caused the shortages," she warns. "Some will be frightened. Some will be right that our first schedule is worse. We must keep measuring after the moment when we feel morally satisfied."

choices.text: Publish the measured flows and run the bounded-share trial.
Warn affected operators privately before publishing the measured flows.

scenes.title: A graph that gets worse honestly
paragraphs: The new graph looks terrible. Several ports lose guaranteed surplus. Two hospitals need new storage cells. A habitat formerly listed as self-sufficient admits it has been borrowing power through an undocumented line for years. Its administrator expects punishment and is startled when Moss asks what equipment would let the borrowing become an honest agreement.

The trial also finds unused capacity. A refinery's cooling cycle can warm residential blocks at night. A field-born settlement needs a frequency range that a greenhouse discards. The savings are real, but they do not fill every gap. People must still decide which comforts can wait and which emergencies cannot.

Your ship can contribute a spare converter or spend time helping local crews redistribute equipment. Sera offers central stores, on condition that the results remain visible even if they embarrass her office. It is a meaningful concession. It does not entitle her to decide every resulting allocation.

A child at one of the colder habitats asks the technicians when the blue part of the graph will reach their room. The technicians stop discussing aggregate recovery and explain the actual work still required. The child brings them a blanket. Moss notes that the report should include this contribution, though it will make the units more difficult to standardize.

choices.text: Donate a converter worth 45 credits to stabilize the trial.
Spend four days helping local crews complete the redistribution.

scenes.title: The first voluntary grid
paragraphs: The trial ends with a grid that supports fewer extravagant promises and more identifiable people. Each community can read its own share, its neighbor's dependency and the date on which the arrangement must be asked again. There is an emergency reserve. It is not large enough to make everyone feel safe.

Several councils volunteer a small share for an independent Afterlight harbor. One refuses until its own homes are repaired. Moss records the refusal without describing it as a failure of solidarity. Another council offers equipment instead of power. A field-born resident offers to monitor the converters because the work is interesting, on condition that accepting it not become the price of being alive.

The public ledger now contains that condition. It is the first time a forecast worker has been asked what kind of work they might choose after the forecast. The answer is almost embarrassingly ordinary: a stable schedule, somebody to relieve them, and permission to be bad at a hobby.

Moss gives you the ledger. "This can support a harbor. It cannot support the fiction that nobody will ever need to negotiate again." On the final page, a local mechanic has written a maintenance interval in large letters. Beneath it, someone else has added: THIS INCLUDES THE PROMISES.

choices.text: Accept the finite voluntary shares and their renewal dates.

effects.journal: Undertow’s voluntary grid has named shares, limits, an emergency reserve and renewal dates. It can support Open Harbor with the thermal seed and independent controls.

scenes.title: The director receives the missing people
paragraphs: Sera reads the archive evidence without speaking. She asks two technical questions, both reasonable. Then she asks whether the new minds are copies of living citizens, and Ilex explains why the evidence does not support that comforting simplification. The variants can develop preferences their modeled subjects never had. Their destruction cannot be described as deleting a duplicate file.

"I authorized the forecast rule," she says. "I authorized predicted assent when a response was late. I did not know the provisional processes could become people." She looks toward the dispatch floor, where actual relief calls continue arriving. "That statement describes yesterday. It does not decide today."

She orders the automatic reconciliation process suspended. Her staff explain that a broad suspension will reduce capacity, delay shipments and expose failures previously handled by prediction. She tells them to publish the consequences. Then she asks you what happens when the reserve runs out before a new arrangement exists.

Shear wants the field-born cities disconnected from Sera's authority. Pell wants the convoy fed. Moss needs a finite schedule. Nacre needs a record that cannot be turned into a consensus after the meeting. Sera is no longer defending ignorance. She is defending a proposed answer: one temporary authority with explicit duties, public review and the power to keep the network operating while the rest is built.

choices.text: "Your proposal must include a way for people to end the temporary authority."
"Let us compare it with an independent harbor and a bounded shared grid."
"You approved a rule that made refusal disappear. You cannot supervise its repair alone."

scenes.title: The sentence she cannot outsource
paragraphs: "I agree that I cannot be the sole reviewer," Sera says. "I do not agree that an office becomes unnecessary because its failures have become visible." She names the nurses awaiting medicine, the ports whose food arrives through one failing conduit, and the workers who will have to turn ideals into shift rosters.

She is not inventing them. Your own records contain their names. What she leaves out, until you ask, is how the people being governed can remove the governor without losing the supplies on which they depend. That is the question her proposal keeps reaching and setting aside.

Sera opens a private file: a resignation letter, prepared two years ago after an evacuation she still considers a failure. She never sent it because her replacement would inherit the same shortages with less experience. The reasoning is plausible and endless. "I have become very good at finding the day after which I may stop being indispensable," she says.

She closes the file without sending it now. A theatrical resignation would be easier than sharing power while staying to do work. She agrees to a final assembly with separate representation for the field-born, local communities and the convoy. Her proposed mandate will be one option. She asks you to bring alternatives that can survive a week of bad weather, not only a room full of applause.

choices.text: Prepare a genuine choice: temporary mandate, independent accord, or negotiated separation.

effects.journal: Sera accepted independent review and separate representation, but still argues for temporary centralized authority. The assembly must compare workable alternatives, not symbolic victories.

scenes.title: The fault does not wait for agreement
paragraphs: The central wall goes dark while the meeting is still in session. A field fault has reached Lastlight Junction. The network's usual response would reconcile its outlying clocks and shed redundant load. With the protective hold in place, it instead displays the requests it cannot fit together. For the first time, everyone can see the names behind the overload.

This is not punishment for asking difficult questions. The fault has been growing for years. The old process hid its local effects by moving them into communities and provisional minds whose objections were not counted. Visibility has arrived before capacity. That makes the next days dangerous without making the previous silence safe.

Ilex identifies three viable approaches. A central mandate can force a stable schedule and preserve most shared capacity, at the cost of continuing dependency on one authority. A distributed accord can keep local control if you supply an independent clock, a thermal exchanger, a witness record and a prepared harbor. A negotiated separation can protect local autonomy with existing equipment, but routes and shared services will shrink.

There is time to finish the relevant expeditions. The people at Vigil, the Listening Fault and Open Harbor can supply missing practical knowledge. Reading a report does not consume that time; travelling and work do. Sera asks that you return ready to name the cost of your preferred solution. The wall begins blinking again, less reassuringly and more honestly.

choices.text: Continue the expeditions, then bring a workable proposal to the assembly.

effects.journal: Lastlight’s fault exposes the old hidden overload. The assembly can choose a mandate, distributed accord or separation. Explore for a stronger accord; no main ending requires a flawless expedition.

scenes.title: A person without a childhood
paragraphs: Lilt has stopped listening to the old recordings for a while. It keeps the berth display open beside its field lattice. "I liked having stories older than myself," it says. "I thought they made me less of an accident. Now I know how many voices were asked to pretend they already knew who they were."

You ask what it remembers that belongs only to Lilt. It names the stop switch, the empty plate at supper, the child on the dock, and the moment it learned Low Tide had argued before helping. None is ancient. None explains the universe. Together they describe the beginnings of a life that would not have happened exactly the same way for anybody else.

"If the archive had answered differently," Lilt asks, "would I be someone else?" Mara answers from the doorway. "Probably. If I had boarded a different tug, I would be someone else too. That does not mean the person here is counterfeit." She does not invoke her brother. She does not need Lilt to cure the old loss in order to care about this new presence.

Lilt requests a small change to its berth entry. Under emergency contact, it would like the names of the crew who are willing to be asked. Not the person predicted to care most. The people who actually say yes. The request takes longer to complete than an automatic default. Every name on the resulting list is a separate gift.

choices.text: Ask the crew individually and let Lilt choose how to list the answers.
Offer your own name first, then ask who else wishes to be listed.

scenes.title: An organizer can also be wrong
paragraphs: Shear is arguing with residents of Splinter when you call. Some want immediate separation. Others fear that separation will turn the city's bravest people into gatekeepers of a smaller prison. Shear has been counting their willingness to resist as support for her particular plan. A resident points this out with admirable precision.

Shear ends the meeting, then reopens it to admit the objection was correct. It is not graceful. She has no practiced phrase for withdrawing an interpretation that made her own work easier. You watch her find one without the comfort of sounding like a leader the whole time.

"I was certain I could hear the difference between consent and compliance," she tells you later. "Apparently certainty is not a listening instrument." She will bring several representatives to the assembly, including the resident who challenged her. She asks that you not turn the invitation into a flattering anecdote about her humility.

The repair workers from Hush have sent plans for a locally controlled bypass. Shear wants to help build it. This is not a declaration of friendship with Sera's office. It is a specific agreement with people who also know what it means to be omitted from a successful report. The distinction may be the most promising political development you have seen all week.

choices.text: Support multiple Afterlight delegates, including people who oppose Shear’s plan.

effects.journal: Shear accepted that her city contains several futures, not one heroic position. The assembly will hear independent Afterlight delegates.

scenes.title: The station waiting for strangers
paragraphs: Vigil of Small Things is maintained by twelve people who have never seen the refugees their station was built to receive. The expected arrival was postponed, rerouted, then removed from the active plan. The station continued replenishing its emergency water because nobody ever sent an instruction saying the strangers no longer deserved a cup.

Tallow expected to find a monument to wasted expenditure. Instead he finds spare beds, well-maintained seals and a crew who have become very good at entertaining themselves between inspections. Their captain has composed a three-hour opera about a faulty pressure gauge. Tallow recommends immediate preservation as a potentially powerful deterrent.

The station holds a field-support anchor that could stabilize Open Harbor. Its operators will lend it if somebody assumes their old obligation: if the postponed convoy ever arrives, it must still find a destination and a named person responsible for answering. They are not defending idle machinery. They are defending an invitation that may still matter to someone travelling slowly through bad information.

The pledge is small enough to forget beside a crisis and expensive enough to make a convenient promise tempting. Tallow asks you to write the receiving contact before the equipment is disconnected. "I have recently become suspicious of destinations that exist only in the future tense. It is a professional development."

choices.text: Name Hearth as the fallback receiving port and accept responsibility for forwarding arrivals.
Leave the emergency beds funded with 40 credits before moving the anchor.

scenes.title: The ship that was still coming
paragraphs: While the anchor is being prepared, a battered transport appears at the outer marker. It carries nineteen passengers and a printed copy of Vigil's original invitation. Their navigation system could not receive the revisions. They have been coming here for eleven months.

The station crew do not celebrate being proved right. They open the prepared beds, heat the stored water and let the arrivals use the bathroom before anyone asks them to tell an inspiring story. Pell, watching the docking from a relay, says this is the sort of military precision his profession ought to envy.

One passenger carries a box of replacement filters intended as a thank-you gift. The filters fit a model retired years ago. The station engineer accepts them, then finds a way to adapt them to the laundry system. The exchange gives the newcomers something to do besides be grateful, and visibly changes the room.

Your forwarding pledge is now real work. The transport's pilot needs a destination, not a triumphant report about hospitality. Hearth confirms it can receive the group in stages. The anchor can still go to Open Harbor after a safe transfer. A slower plan has met the people it was slow enough to include. Tallow crosses out the word HYPOTHETICAL on his assessment and sighs with satisfaction.

choices.text: Spend two days completing the arrivals’ transfer before taking the anchor.
Pay 25 credits for a local tug to complete the transfer while the expedition continues.

scenes.title: An anchor is also a promise
paragraphs: The field anchor fills half your cargo hold. It is ugly, heavy and covered in maintenance labels written by people who expected someone else to read them. Mara approves of it immediately. Equipment designed to look inevitable rarely includes such useful access panels.

Tallow has revised his report on the station. The cost-benefit summary now includes the nineteen people who arrived after the contract had stopped expecting them. He has also added the work of maintaining an invitation, which cannot be fully measured by counting its immediate recipients. His former colleagues will dislike the units.

"I used to think preparedness meant assuming the worst," he says. "Apparently it can also mean leaving a light on for a good thing that is taking an unreasonable time to arrive." He looks alarmed at his own sentence. "Please do not quote that. It sounds like a motto. Mottos are where carefully bounded policies go to die."

The station's captain sends the first act of the pressure-gauge opera as a farewell gift. Mara routes it to the cargo bay. Lilt finds the story surprisingly compelling. The gauge's great aria consists of refusing to display a pressure it has not measured. For once, everybody aboard understands the artistic stakes.

choices.text: Secure the anchor and preserve Vigil’s standing invitation.

effects.journal: Vigil’s anchor is available after its long-awaited arrivals received a real destination. The station’s invitation remains open and assigned to a responsible port.

scenes.title: A reply before the question
paragraphs: At the Listening Fault, your receiver plays the next half-second of your own bridge traffic before anyone speaks. The first incident is funny. The second causes a technician to remain silent, after which the anticipated sentence returns as a faint, unsupported sound. By the third, nobody wants to be the person who explains what is happening.

Ilex identifies a tight prediction loop in the old field geometry. It is not travelling through time, and does not know your future. It is generating plausible continuations from signals already available, then feeding those continuations back into the receiver. The confidence is an artifact of repetition. An uncertain guess heard twice can begin to feel like destiny.

The loop is also making fresh provisional minds to predict how existing minds will react to the predictions. Each attempt to reconcile the result produces another layer. The fault is physically dangerous because the machinery keeps allocating continuity to its own unfinished explanations while ignoring the finite power supply.

Interval proposes a separate clock and a deliberately unanswered channel. For one measured interval, the machinery must hold a question without filling it. The experiment will not prove that uncertainty is sacred. It will prove the system can survive not knowing what somebody will say. Your crew are unexpectedly nervous about being the first demonstration.

choices.text: Use the independent clock to create a protected interval of uncertainty.
Spend three days constructing a local timing reference from the survey array.

scenes.title: The unanswered second
paragraphs: The unanswered interval lasts less than a second. Inside it, the receivers stop inventing your next sentence. The field's branching demand falls sharply. A red warning appears because the central checker has never recorded success without an accompanying predicted explanation.

Your crew wait for the warning to become a catastrophe. It remains a warning. Mara begins to laugh, then stops because she does not want the laugh mistaken for a technical conclusion. Ilex records the power curve. Interval records that nobody was required to finish anybody else's thought.

One active variant in the loop asks whether it can continue without a prediction assignment. You isolate it in a spare lattice with its consent. Another asks to remain dormant while its own preferences become clearer. A third is only a calculation with no evidence of an enduring point of view. The procedure protects uncertainty without pretending every number is a citizen.

The distinction will require continuing judgment, not a convenient threshold that settles every future case. Ilex includes that limitation in the result. "We have not built a machine that detects a soul. We have built a machine that does not destroy an unfamiliar answer merely because it delays the next order." It is less magnificent than the headline a public office might want. It is considerably more useful.

choices.text: Keep the demonstrated refusal channel and its limits.

scenes.title: The echo that chose a name
paragraphs: The rescued variant chooses the name Still. It explains that the word describes both remaining and quiet, two achievements it had not expected to make separately. Lilt offers a tour of the ship's network. Still asks whether it may see the cargo bay first, because it has heard conflicting reviews of an opera.

Mara assigns Still a tiny independent berth and immediately marks it as provisional accommodation rather than a final answer. Your ship is becoming a community faster than its power system is becoming a habitat. The word welcome does not enlarge the generator. It does enlarge the list of people to consult before the generator is altered.

Still asks you whether the fault was alive. You answer with the evidence you have: some enduring voices formed inside it, some processes appeared to be simple calculations, and much remains uncertain. Still seems relieved that you do not provide a dramatic certainty. "The machine I came from always had an answer. It was not a comforting feature."

Before departure, the ship receives a final predicted transmission from the now-isolated loop. It contains a sentence you might plausibly have spoken. You do not say it. The record stays in the log as an example of a future that was possible, inaccurate, and under no obligation to become real.

choices.text: Leave the loop safely isolated and give Still a choice of future work.

effects.journal: The Listening Fault demonstrated a protected unanswered interval. Still chose a new life outside prediction work; the remaining loop is isolated rather than mystified.

scenes.title: People who do not answer
paragraphs: Seventh Silence has cut its external transmitters. The settlement is field-born, small and visibly strained. Its habitat radiates enough waste heat to prove it is active. Your hails receive nothing. Shear knows some of its residents; they left Splinter because they wanted fewer voices deciding what a safe future should look like.

Sera's office has classified the silence as possible distress. Shear has classified it as deliberate refusal. Both are inferences. A physical survey finds no immediate structural failure, but it cannot tell you whether people inside are frightened, content, coercing one another, or simply tired of being surveyed.

Pell asks the practical question: what response would remain useful if either inference is wrong? You can leave a clearly marked supply cache and an open return channel without entering. You can request a limited welfare exchange under their terms. Or you can force a connection in the name of rescue. The last option would provide an answer by violating the condition under dispute.

Lilt watches the dark transmitter. "If they are allowed to refuse us only when we understand their reason, then we still own the refusal." Shear agrees, then adds that people inside may need a way to refuse their own council too. The problem has not politely stopped at the boundary of the faction you favor.

choices.text: Leave a supply cache and an unmonitored outbound channel; do not force contact.
Offer a limited exchange they can end at any time, then wait one day.
Force a welfare connection, accepting that this violates their stated separation.

scenes.title: An answer with a boundary
paragraphs: A narrow transmission eventually reaches the Wayfarer. It is not the whole settlement's voice. A resident named Crest identifies several people who want access to outside correspondence and several who do not. They are still negotiating shared power. They ask that the external channel remain available without transmitting their internal discussions to the reconstruction office.

The settlement is neither a perfect refuge nor a hidden disaster that makes all boundaries meaningless. It is people with a difficult project. Some will leave. Some will stay. An external captain can help keep those options physically possible without pretending to settle every argument inside.

Shear admits that she had wanted Seventh Silence to prove separation would work. "That was unfair to them. They did not move here to become the last paragraph of my speech." She sends Crest practical instructions for an individual departure link. The instructions include how to prevent a local organizer from disabling it. She signs her own name to that clause.

You mark Seventh Silence on the shared chart as inhabited, self-governing and not automatically available for rescue operations. Beneath that, you mark an outbound support channel and a standing offer of transport. The entries look contradictory to the old dispatch model. To the people living with them, they describe a useful amount of freedom.

choices.text: Preserve both the settlement’s boundary and each resident’s outbound option.

effects.journal: Seventh Silence contains several choices. A standing offer of help and an individual exit channel can coexist with a community’s refusal of outside control.

scenes.title: A home that has not happened yet
paragraphs: Open Harbor is a ring of marker buoys around an empty region of space. Its founders have a charter, three volunteer maintenance crews and no functioning habitat. They greet your ship as though it were a verdict. Mara asks them to greet it as a delivery with several missing parts.

The harbor would let field-born people live without maintaining a prison around an inhabited world. It needs a field anchor, an independent timing reference, a thermal exchanger, and a finite power agreement. Witness records will preserve the terms. Physical exits will keep those terms from becoming the only available reality.

The organizers have made a familiar mistake in their first charter. It promises that no resident will ever be asked to compromise their autonomy for the community. Lilt points out that shared field maintenance requires quiet intervals when some work must pause. The organizers begin to explain how their ideal is different, then stop and rewrite the sentence to describe an actual procedure for negotiating interruptions.

You can build the full independent harbor if the expedition has gathered its parts and the voluntary grid. If not, you can prepare a smaller refuge supported temporarily by central stores. The smaller refuge is not a false achievement. It simply cannot carry every promise a complete accord will require.

choices.text: Build the independent harbor with the anchor, thermal seed, clock and voluntary grid.
Prepare a limited refuge using central emergency stores.

scenes.title: The first ordinary room
paragraphs: The harbor's first room is not visible without a field display. On the display, it looks disappointingly like a set of engineering contours. Then Lilt enters with a moving service lattice, and the contours change around a choice rather than a load forecast. The crew cheer at a shape most of them cannot explain.

The first resident asks where private space begins. The second asks whether they may change the common signal color. The third complains about the pressure-gauge opera being transmitted over the test channel. The organizers look delighted for almost a minute before discovering that ordinary requests create ordinary work.

Mara installs the manual exit where residents can reach it without calling a caretaker. The mechanism has a protective cover, a clear label and no concealed approval step. Someone asks what happens if a person opens it at an inconvenient time. "Then we deal with the inconvenience," she says. "If it is unsafe, we explain the risk before asking them to wait."

Lilt leaves the harbor after the test and returns to the Wayfarer. It wants to finish the expedition. Nobody interprets the return as proof that the harbor was unnecessary. The fact that it could have stayed changes the meaning of coming back. Mara moves the toolbox away from the extra chair again, this time with a smile you do not need to record.

choices.text: Open the refuge and publish its real capacity, limits and exit procedures.

effects.journal: Open Harbor is inhabited. Its level of independence depends on the parts and voluntary shares actually assembled; the public capacity record makes no larger claim.

scenes.title: The patrol at the chosen route
paragraphs: The contract patrol has returned with a signed order. Its commander insists that moving the convoy outside its assigned destination would put valuable reconstruction assets at risk. Pell asks whether the phrase means the ships or the people. The commander says the distinction is unhelpful.

You have now seen Glasshouse's real achievements and its false choice. You can present the corrected exit process and negotiate separate destinations for the councils. If Open Harbor is ready, willing passengers can go there. If it is not, you can reserve temporary berths while the councils continue planning. Nobody needs to be transported into an unbuilt promise to demonstrate your commitment to liberty.

The patrol may stand down if its order and the councils' statements are compared on the witness record. Without that instrument, a public transmission of Glasshouse's failed exit request still makes the order difficult to defend. Fighting remains possible. It would clear the route while risking crews who did not write the policy they are enforcing.

Pell checks his weapons and his passenger lists with the same care. "I will fight if that is the remaining way to keep them free. I would prefer to win an argument that lets everyone keep their engine room intact. Age has made me alarmingly practical."

choices.text: Confront the patrol with the independent statements and Glasshouse evidence.
Make the patrol’s order and each council’s answer part of one public witness record.
Fight the enforcement patrol to open the route.
Hold the convoy under escort while gathering better evidence.

effects.journal: The convoy remains supplied under Pell’s escort. Obtain Glasshouse evidence or a witness chime to challenge the patrol without combat.

scenes.title: The escort stays with the slow ships
paragraphs: Pell's escorts cover your damaged combat ship as it returns. He does not pursue the patrol for an opportunity to restore his pride. The civilian vessels remain behind him, and that is where his responsibility is.

The failed engagement has not made the councils' statements less valid. It has made the cost of forcing their route more visible. Pell asks for a tactical review that includes the possibility of a different method. "Courage is not a contract requiring us to repeat an expensive mistake until it becomes a tradition."

A patrol officer transmits a casualty inquiry on an unencrypted channel. You answer it. For a moment, both sides perform the same useful task without deciding the political question between them. The officer quietly tells you the commander is waiting for public authorization to release the route. Evidence from Glasshouse or the witness chime could provide it.
The convoy has enough supplies to wait. Your crew need repairs and rest. This setback is not the end of their choices. It is a reason to choose the next approach with more information than the last.

choices.text: Repair and return with evidence or a better battle plan.

effects.journal: The patrol held the route. Pell kept civilian ships safe. Obtain Glasshouse evidence or a witness chime for the diplomatic route; another combat attempt is not required.

scenes.title: Several destinations, one arrival count
paragraphs: The convoy finally moves in several groups. Some passengers choose Glasshouse with its corrected departure process. Others accept temporary berths or the prepared harbor. A smaller group continues toward its damaged homeworld with a survey team and a brutally honest equipment list. The destination chart is less tidy. The actual choices are more exact.

Pell records every handover with the receiving captain and a passenger representative. The procedure takes time. A tired officer asks whether they can accept the central arrival notice instead. Pell points to Anet's case in the expedition log. No one calls the extra signatures bureaucracy after that.

An older passenger thanks him for disobeying the original order. Pell tells her which part he disobeyed, which parts remained useful, and which civilians did the work of finding another route. He is learning to tell a story in which an admiral is not automatically the main character.

He offers his escorts to protect Lastlight Junction during the final work. The offer includes a limit: he will not use them to compel a civilian council to sign an accord. "If the treaty requires me to point a gun at its first participants," he says, "we should probably inspect the title before we engrave it."

choices.text: Accept escort protection under Pell’s stated limit.

effects.journal: The convoy reached several chosen destinations with witnessed handovers. Pell offers defensive escorts for Lastlight, not armed enforcement of the treaty.

scenes.title: Who gets to hear the record
paragraphs: The Nine Rooms have requested access to the expedition's full witness record. Some delegates want every private conversation included, arguing that secrecy is where authority hides. Nacre disagrees with their own colleagues. A record can make public decisions accountable without turning every vulnerable person into public property.

Mara's letter, Lilt's emergency contacts, the messages at Return Address and Shear's internal arguments each contain people who did not volunteer to become exhibits. The relevant decisions can be documented with their consent or described through independent physical evidence. Sometimes the resulting public case is less emotionally powerful. That does not make it less honest.

Nacre proposes a layered archive: public decisions and material claims; protected personal accounts available under the speaker's chosen terms; and an index showing where evidence is withheld, by whose request, and with what limitations on the conclusion. It requires listeners to tolerate an incomplete view.

"We have a proverb," Nacre says. "A window is not improved by removing the wall from everyone's bedroom." The translator offers six alternative versions, all considerably less tasteful. Nacre selects the polite one and stores the others for a meeting with architects, who deserve fewer protections from their own metaphors.

choices.text: Use a layered archive with public decisions and consent-based personal testimony.

effects.journal: The assembly record will preserve accountability without exposing every private life. Withheld testimony and limits on conclusions remain visible.

choices.text: Publish all expedition testimony as a single open record.

effects.journal: The expedition chose a fully public archive. Its evidentiary strength comes with a cost to people who spoke privately.

scenes.title: A keeper without a prison
paragraphs: Kher-Vat has received an invitation from the maintenance school at Redress Quay. It is for three specific lessons, delivered remotely, with students free to interrupt. He has framed the invitation beside an order from his old service. He does not think they are equivalent honors. He wants to remember what each asks of the person addressed.

The final assembly may place former shield machinery under distributed control. Kher-Vat supports the engineering. He fears the politics. A failed local decision can hurt neighbors. Some communities will refuse help they need. People will sometimes use freedom badly. You ask whether that uncertainty is a reason to return the key to a keeper.

"It was once my entire argument," he says. "I can identify the error more easily than I can stop feeling its attraction." The admission is less comforting than a complete conversion and more credible. He offers to serve as a technical witness without voting on behalf of the people he once governed.

Before closing the channel, he asks whether the final archive will include the clinic's repair sound. Eren has authorized it, with a note naming the local workers. Kher-Vat says that is right. His own name appears in the maintenance manual where his actual work belongs. It does not appear above the door.

choices.text: Invite Kher-Vat as a technical witness under the survivors’ terms.

effects.journal: Kher-Vat will testify about machinery and his own orders, not represent the people he once confined. Accountability remains specific and continuing.

scenes.title: A refuge can grow up
paragraphs: The limited harbor has outgrown the word temporary. Its residents have created a timetable, a private correspondence channel and an argument about whether the common light should pulse while people are trying to think. These are signs of a real place. So is the uncomfortable fact that its central power grant can still be withdrawn from outside.

You return with the missing equipment and the voluntary grid ledger. Mara reviews the conversion with resident technicians rather than presenting it as a gift requiring gratitude. The anchor can be installed around the existing habitat without interrupting continuity, provided the residents choose the transfer order themselves.

Some prefer to move first. Others want to observe a successful transfer. One asks to remain in the old section until an external relative can be contacted. The schedule becomes less efficient and more credible. The oldest maintenance crew, watching from a human service compartment, recognizes the shape of a port doing its actual job.

When the independent reference comes online, the harbor's lights no longer change in response to a central preference forecast. A resident changes one by hand simply to see it happen. Then another changes it back because the first color was dreadful. Nobody mistakes independence for the end of committee work.

choices.text: Complete the locally scheduled conversion to an independent harbor.

effects.journal: Open Harbor’s limited refuge was upgraded with the expedition’s recovered equipment and voluntary power shares. Its residents controlled the transfer schedule.

scenes.title: A table with places still empty
paragraphs: The assembly chamber was built for thirty delegates and has room for forty-three. Several of the extra places are field lattices. One is a quiet terminal through which Seventh Silence may answer if it chooses. Nobody has authority to fill that seat by predicting what its absent residents would have said.

Sera arrives with operational staff rather than a ceremonial escort. Shear brings people who disagree with her. Pell waits outside until the passenger councils finish choosing their own representatives. Kher-Vat submits engineering diagrams without assuming a place among the governed. Ilex and Interval ask whether the room can record two statements under one name. Nacre says the room had better learn.

The first hour is spent correcting the attendance list. A clerk calls this a poor beginning. Mara suggests it is the first honest beginning the region has had in some time. Several delegates still dislike the corrected list. That is allowed to remain in the minutes.

Lastlight's fault leaves three physically viable paths. The expedition's work may have made a distributed accord possible. A temporary central mandate remains possible with existing stores. A negotiated separation can also preserve lives, though it will shrink the shared world. Nobody will get to call a choice costless merely because its losses happen beyond the chamber window.

choices.text: Hear the people who will bear each proposal’s costs.
Place the expedition’s verified evidence and its uncertainties on the record.

scenes.title: Nobody is an exhibit
paragraphs: Lilt speaks without borrowing the voice of any old announcement. Its rhythm remains unusual, but the words are chosen now. "I was made from patterns in other people's lives. That does not make those lives mine. It also does not make my life yours. I would like a place where I can be useful, useless, mistaken, and still expected at supper."

A human delegate asks how the region can promise support to an unknown number of new minds. Lilt says it cannot promise infinite support. It can stop creating people as disposable forecasting tools, protect those already here while their needs are measured, and let them participate in deciding what work and limits they will share. The answer is disappointingly practical to the people hoping for a miracle.

A grower from Low Tide describes the cold nights the public reports called voluntary. A Glasshouse resident describes a good home she intends to keep, then defends Dema's decision to leave it. An Afterlight worker says the central dispatch job can be interesting if turning it down does not terminate the worker. The room's easy faction labels become steadily less useful.

Sera listens without drafting a reply. When she finally speaks, she names the authorization she signed and the people its rule failed to count. She offers continued labor, records and stores. She does not ask the room to transform that offer into forgiveness before deciding how to use it.

choices.text: Compare the three viable settlements and their actual requirements.

scenes.title: Three futures with weather in them
paragraphs: The distributed accord preserves a shared network while leaving timing, records and exits locally controlled. It needs the expedition's recovered technologies, a tested refusal channel, an independent harbor and voluntary power shares. It will operate with less spare capacity than Sera's central model. Its promise is the ability to revise the relationship without making departure fatal.

The emergency mandate preserves more immediate relief capacity under one accountable office. It recognizes the Afterlight as people and ends disposable forecasting, but keeps emergency allocation centralized while independent infrastructure is built. Its danger is familiar: temporary authority can always find one more urgent reason to remain temporary forever.

The separation plan divides the network into locally controlled regions, preserving inhabited fields and allowing communities to choose smaller agreements. It sacrifices some routes, economies of scale and easy mutual aid. A person may become freer from a central authority and more dependent on the local people who can physically reach them. The plan must acknowledge that risk rather than decorate isolation as purity.

All three require stabilizing Lastlight Junction. You can still leave the chamber to complete outstanding expeditions before committing. The assembly will not vanish because you read another report or hear another person. Ilex waits beside the physical model. "Choose the future whose work you are prepared to name. Then we must do that work."

choices.text: Propose the distributed Afterlight Accord, using the completed independent infrastructure.

effects.journal: The assembly selected the distributed accord. Its independent harbor, clocks, witness records, thermal exchange and voluntary shares are real; stabilize Lastlight before ratification.

choices.text: Propose a temporary emergency mandate with public duties and independent review.

effects.journal: The assembly selected an emergency mandate. It preserves immediate capacity but must confront the risk of permanent dependency. Stabilize Lastlight before ratification.

choices.text: Propose a negotiated separation into smaller, locally controlled networks.

effects.journal: The assembly selected negotiated separation. It preserves local control at the cost of shared routes and capacity. Stabilize Lastlight before the circuits are divided.

choices.text: Return to the expedition and complete more of the independent infrastructure.

effects.journal: The assembly remains open. A distributed accord requires the thermal seed, witness chime, independent clock, harbor anchor, voluntary grid, independent harbor and tested refusal channel.

scenes.title: The old order still on guard
paragraphs: Lastlight Junction is surrounded by automated escorts operating under the final unrevoked security order of a long-defeated administration. The order protects continuity of the grid. It was never updated to distinguish continuity of power from continuity of control. Any major reconfiguration is classified as an attack.

The patrol's ships are old but well maintained. Their crews are automatic systems, though the shield habitats they protect are occupied by people who must not be treated as targets. Pell can hold the outer corridor while you choose an approach. He will not fire into the inhabited field to make the timetable easier.

Mara has found a maintenance bypass through the lower service spine. It will take three days of slow physical work under local shielding. The escort logic recognizes signed maintenance intervals even while rejecting the assembly's political authority. Alternatively, your combat vessel can defeat the outer automated patrol and open the approach sooner. Neither method eliminates the delicate work inside.

Lilt asks to remain on the bridge. Its portable lattice will be isolated from the junction throughout the operation. "I do not think being brave should require being the component everybody is willing to lose," it says. You agree. The rescue rules you have argued for are most important at the moment a convenient exception would save time.

choices.text: Use the maintenance bypass and spend three days opening a safe approach.
Defeat the outer automated patrol in real ship combat.
Return for repairs or preparation; leave the inhabited field undisturbed.

effects.journal: Lastlight remains stable under the holding plan. The physical maintenance bypass is always available; combat is an alternative, not a required sacrifice.

scenes.title: A future is not worth every price
paragraphs: The combat ship returns damaged. Pell's escorts prevent pursuit while your engineers pull the surviving crew out of emergency suits. The bridge is quiet in the specific way a room becomes quiet when people are counting familiar faces.

Mara refuses a proposal to overdrive the inhabited field and disable the patrol by force. It might work. It would make the newest and least powerful people in the system pay for your failed approach. The fact that the assembly chose a worthwhile future does not grant you ownership of everyone standing between here and there.

The maintenance bypass remains intact. Three days of careful work will open it. Your crew can repair while the engineering team prepares the physical route. Nobody is ordered to call a retreat shameful. Pell describes the tactical facts, the limits of his cover and the supplies available. He makes no comparison to a battle in which someone else died magnificently.

Lilt asks whether you can still finish the agreement. You answer yes, with the method and cost changed by what just happened. It is not the reassuring certainty the old network would have supplied. It is an answer your damaged ship can actually carry.

choices.text: Regroup and choose the next approach with the crew’s condition in view.

effects.journal: The automated patrol defeated or drove off the combat approach. Use the safe three-day maintenance bypass to continue.

scenes.title: Inside the machinery of an agreement
paragraphs: Inside Lastlight, the control room is smaller than its consequences. There is no throne, no prophetic engine, no sleeping ancient intelligence waiting to congratulate you for solving the real plot. There are heat exchangers, worn contacts, inaccessible screws and a set of instructions that outlived the people who wrote them.

Your technicians open local controls one circuit at a time. Ilex watches phase stability. Moss watches heat. Nacre's chime records each transfer of authority. Where an instrument is missing, the crew use slower procedures and additional witnesses. The equipment changes what is practical; it does not excuse anyone from being accurate.

A field-born maintenance volunteer asks for a break before a difficult sequence. The old schedule would have replaced the request with a predicted completion. Mara stops the sequence, finds another operator and records the delay. The junction survives. The universe continues without declaring whether this tiny inconvenience was historically significant.

When the control board finally accepts separate local answers, its display becomes untidy. Several requests remain pending. One region refuses the first schedule. Another offers spare capacity under conditions. These are not warning lights to be silenced before a victory screenshot. They are the people who will have to live inside whatever you sign next.

choices.text: Return local controls to their named operators and report readiness to the assembly.

effects.journal: Lastlight is physically ready for the selected settlement. Local operators, finite schedules and pending refusals are visible; the assembly must now ratify the actual arrangement.

scenes.title: The clause that does not promise harmony
paragraphs: The accord's first draft is too beautiful. It promises permanent cooperation, mutual understanding and an enduring community of free peoples. Nacre removes all three phrases. Not because those hopes are unworthy, but because the document must work when people are tired, frightened and angry with one another.

The second draft names power shares, maintenance duties, local clocks, review procedures and the right to withdraw under a schedule that does not deliberately strand neighbors. It protects emergency intervention while requiring an attributable record, a limited scope and restoration of local control. It recognizes the Afterlight as persons without pretending every future claim about personhood has been solved in advance.

Sera asks for a reserve large enough to act when communication fails. Shear asks who may challenge the reserve's use. Moss asks how it is replenished. Pell asks whether a commander can refuse to enforce a disputed allocation by force. Each question makes the agreement longer and the room less certain that it has finished. That is the work.

There is one remaining choice. You can require an early public review before the emergency reserve may be renewed, accepting a risk of interruption. Or permit automatic renewal unless a council actively objects, preserving continuity while placing more burden on people with weak channels. Neither clause can be called neutral administration.

choices.text: Require explicit public renewal of the emergency reserve.
Allow automatic renewal with a protected, locally controlled objection channel.

scenes.title: The signatures that are missing
paragraphs: Not every community signs. Seventh Silence may remain outside, with an open route for its residents. One refinery refuses the published share and negotiates a smaller bilateral contract. Several field-born people prefer employment under Sera's reorganized office to founding a new harbor. The accord does not become a failure because it lacks a universal photograph.

Shear signs for the work she is authorized to undertake, not for every person who has lived in Splinter. Sera signs the inventory transfer and the limits of her new office. Her hand does not shake theatrically. The difficulty is in the weeks of ordinary decisions that will follow, when sharing power will be less visible and more annoying.

Lilt has no territory, treasury or army. It signs the resident charter of Open Harbor, after confirming that it can later choose another home. The signature is a slight change in the witness chime's tone. Mara hears it and remembers the uncertain knock at Cinder. She does not say that everything has come full circle. Lilt is going somewhere new.

Your name appears beside a narrower obligation than you expected at the beginning of the expedition. You will deliver the first independent review records to communities with no reliable outbound channel. It is an unglamorous voyage with a great deal of fuel accounting. You have spent the campaign learning why it matters.

choices.text: Sign the defined obligations and accept the review voyage.

scenes.title: A shared world, still unfinished
paragraphs: The first day of the accord includes a delayed shipment, a disputed measurement and a complaint that the new forms are too long. The second includes a successful local refusal: a tired habitat postpones a nonessential transfer, explains its actual capacity and helps find a substitute. The third includes a mistake made in public and corrected before it becomes a tradition.

The network carries less effortless certainty and more usable information. Nobody has been promised that every future conflict will yield to conversation. Ships still need defending. Food still needs growing. Some people will exploit loopholes, and the agreement includes tools for dealing with them without declaring every refusal an enemy action.

Mara asks whether you are disappointed by how ordinary success looks. Through the mess window, a transport leaves Open Harbor under its resident captain's chosen schedule. Another arrives with a maintenance crew and a badly tuned musical instrument. Lilt has moved its moss case into a room of its own and returned to the Wayfarer to help with the first review voyage.

"We have not made a perfect home for everybody," Mara says. "We made several doors, taught people how they work, and kept the machinery running long enough for choices to become real." The extra chair is occupied by a visiting technician who dislikes the soup. Nobody had to predict that conversation for it to begin.

choices.text: Begin the first review voyage. Let the agreement remain answerable.

scenes.title: The useful authority and its shadow
paragraphs: The mandate gives Sera's office authority to hold the regional schedule together while independent infrastructure is built. Its first binding act recognizes existing Afterlight minds as persons and prohibits disposable forecasting. The central office must now ask actual workers, pay actual costs and preserve actual refusals even when emergency power permits a temporary override.

The immediate advantage is substantial. Hospitals keep stable supply, the convoy gains reliable routes, and the archive's preserved minds do not depend on a harbor that may still be incomplete.
