The cost is also substantial: the same institution that distributes necessities remains able to decide which local choices create an unacceptable emergency.

Sera proposes an independent review board with access to every operational record. Shear insists the board must be able to remove the director without interrupting basic support. The staff demonstrate how difficult that separation will be with the present machinery. Difficult does not mean unnecessary. It means the authority needs a funded obligation to make itself replaceable.

You can insist on a fixed expiry requiring public reauthorization, even if preparations are incomplete. Or permit the board to extend the mandate when it certifies a continuing emergency. The first risks an abrupt political crisis. The second risks a gradual future in which an emergency becomes the region's normal form of government.

choices.text: Set a fixed expiry and fund the machinery needed to transfer authority.
Permit extensions only by an independent board with published evidence.

scenes.title: The people who vote against being saved this way
paragraphs: Several Afterlight delegates oppose the mandate. They do not oppose medicine reaching hospitals or the preservation of their own neighbors. They oppose making survival depend on an office whose power they cannot individually escape. Sera acknowledges the distinction in the record. It remains a real disagreement, not a misunderstanding solved by a respectful tone.

Shear negotiates protected settlements with local refusal channels and a guaranteed route to review. The central office accepts these limits, though its schedulers warn that they reduce efficiency. People at the edge of the network will still have to work harder to make their objections heard than people in the main dispatch room.

Lilt chooses to assist the transition as a paid communications worker. It reserves the right to leave that job. Sera signs the contract in person, then makes sure the next worker will not require the same ceremony. A good example is useful; a repeatable procedure is better.

You are asked to witness the first allocation order issued under the new mandate. It contains an emergency transfer, the reason for it, the people affected and a date for returning control. It is better than the old order. Whether that improvement grows or hardens into a reassuring story will depend on work that no ending scene can do for the region.

choices.text: Record the dissent and guarantee its protected route to the review board.
Prioritize immediate operations, with dissent recorded for the first scheduled review.

scenes.title: A winter kept warm
paragraphs: The mandate's first winter begins with lights staying on in places the distributed plan could not yet have supported. Sera's office works longer shifts with fewer miraculous forecasts. Its success is real and no longer free of named costs. The preserved variants choose jobs, dormancy, study and, occasionally, work nobody has thought to fund yet.

The new review board meets in a room outside central dispatch. Its members discover that access to records is different from the time and expertise needed to read them. Local councils request training. Some receive it quickly. Others must insist. The region has gained safeguards and retained a powerful center; both descriptions belong in its history.

Sera sends you a copy of the old resignation letter, this time with no claim that sending it would solve anything. Beside it is the funded transfer plan required by the mandate. "The important document is the second one," she writes. "Please return when its dates arrive. I expect to have excellent reasons why they should move."

Mara reads the message and checks your fuel reserves. The next voyage will be an inspection, not a liberation battle. It may be less exciting. It may be how this choice avoids becoming the lesson every character in the old war should have taught the region already.

choices.text: Accept the inspection duty and keep the mandate’s limits on the public chart.

scenes.title: Smaller worlds with real edges
paragraphs: The separation plan begins with an inventory of dependencies, not a declaration that nobody owes anybody anything. The circuits will divide along lines chosen by their inhabitants where possible. Where geography and machinery make that impossible, temporary shared services will remain under explicit contracts.

Some field-born communities gain direct control of the habitats keeping them alive. Some human settlements lose convenient routes to specialized medicine. Several formerly poor contributors retain power they had been sending into indefinite emergencies elsewhere. The distribution is neither simple liberation nor universal loss. It is a new map of who can reach whom.

Sera opposes the scale of the division but supplies the engineering teams required to keep it from becoming a catastrophe. Shear insists that her own city include individual exit rights. Pell warns that smaller escort zones create gaps in protection. Moss names the seed shipments that must continue across political boundaries if the first season is to succeed.

You must choose what connective tissue to preserve. A limited public corridor will consume scarce capacity and require continuing negotiation. A cleaner separation will give local systems more independent reserve, but make future contact slower and more dependent on captains willing to travel. Neither choice can truthfully be sold as the end of dependency.

choices.text: Preserve a narrow public corridor for correspondence, medicine and voluntary travel.
Prioritize independent local reserves; future links will require new bilateral agreements.

scenes.title: The people between the new borders
paragraphs: Pell organizes the last large shared convoy before the new boundaries take effect. Its passengers are not neatly divided by political preference. Some are moving toward relatives. Some are leaving employers. Some want to try a place whose risks they have chosen rather than remain in a safer place whose rules they cannot change.

A family asks him to prevent an adult son from joining a distant Afterlight workshop. They fear he will never return. Pell explains the route, the communication delays and the very real possibility that the family will dislike the result. Then he lets the son board. He has learned from Glasshouse that a loving objection can still become a locked door.

Shear's city opens an independent receiver and discovers that running a public channel includes spam, insults and people asking questions already answered three times. She delegates the work, badly at first, then accepts criticism from a technician who did not join the city to admire her leadership.

The final shared ledger includes continuing obligations to those unable to travel. They are not abandoned because a vote changed the map around them. Local authorities inherit named duties and public records, along with the uncomfortable knowledge that a distant expedition may return to compare the promises with the rooms where people actually live.

choices.text: Preserve individual exits and public obligations across the new boundaries.

scenes.title: The distance people chose
paragraphs: The shared network grows quieter as the circuits separate. Some communities celebrate. Others count the services they will have to rebuild. A few discover that the local authority they preferred to the distant one can also become difficult to challenge. The exit clauses and witness records matter immediately, which is less romantic than everyone hoped and more useful than everyone feared.

The Afterlight cities survive as several different projects. Some trade with human ports. Some retreat into quiet. Some keep a central service contract because that is the choice their residents actually made. Nobody is entitled to erase those last communities from the story because their decision complicates the triumph of separation.

Mara recalculates the Wayfarer's next route. It will take longer now. The ship will carry letters, spare parts and invitations whose recipients may decline. She places the extra chair where it will not block the cargo access. There is more freight on this voyage and less assurance that a destination will still answer when you arrive.

Lilt looks at the new map. "It has more edges," it says. "That means there are more places to meet." Then it asks whether you can afford the fuel. You appreciate the order of the questions. Hope is allowed to travel with an invoice, provided neither is mistaken for the whole journey.

choices.text: Begin the longer voyage between the newly independent communities.

scenes.title: The smallest review
paragraphs: Before the final trip to the assembly, Mara asks the crew to review the expedition's own decisions. Not the heroic highlights. The emergency disconnection at The Unwritten. The power used at Cinder. The private messages opened or protected. The people whose time you treated as available because your own mission seemed important.

The discussion is uncomfortable and lacks a villain. Several choices were defensible. Some were made before the evidence became clear. A few could have been made better even with what you knew. The crew write down which procedures should change and who will be responsible for changing them.

Mara does not call this proof that your expedition is uniquely virtuous. "Everyone likes an accountable authority until they are asked to account for the thing they were proud of." She puts the report in the same archive as Sera's authorizations. If your proposed future cannot tolerate that placement, it is probably too fragile to survive its first winter.

The last entry concerns the extra chair. It has been moved, borrowed, occupied by a toolbox and used as a drying rack. The crew decide to keep it. Its purpose is no longer to promise that every unexpected arrival will fit. Its purpose is to make the first response to an arrival something other than a calculation of where they can be sent away.

choices.text: Publish the expedition’s own decisions under the same standards as everyone else’s.

effects.journal: The expedition reviewed its own emergency actions and private-data choices. Its record is subject to the standards it asks the region to adopt.

scenes.title: A story without a final owner
paragraphs: Lilt has been composing a record of the expedition in its own words. It asks permission to quote you, then asks how to describe the times when your words and actions did not match. You tell it to describe them accurately. It asks for the instruction in writing. Mara laughs hard enough to spill a little soup.

The draft gives too much space to meals and maintenance. At least, that is the navigation officer's opinion. Lilt considers the moment when a crew member first asked it to lower the common music volume as important as the great archive revelation. "It meant I was allowed to be inconvenient in an ordinary way," it explains.

It has not chosen a title. The Afterlight Accord sounds impressive, but people may mistake the agreement for the end of the story. The Extra Chair sounds small, but perhaps that is an advantage. It keeps both titles for now. A person can hold two possibilities without being reconciled into the one a forecast prefers.

Outside the bridge window, a maintenance shuttle approaches under its own pilot's control. It transmits a request, waits, receives an actual answer and comes alongside. You have seen this happen a hundred times. After this expedition, the little interval between the request and the reply contains more than it used to.

choices.text: Give Lilt permission to tell its own story, including disagreements with yours.

effects.journal: Lilt is writing its own account of the voyage. The expedition’s official record will not be the only version people can read.

scenes.title: The room that remembers badly
paragraphs: Nacre invites you into a room their public architectural tour does not include. Its walls are uneven. The main chord drifts sharp whenever the temperature changes. A younger architect would be embarrassed to sign it. Nacre signed it twice, first as an apprentice and later as the person who chose not to rebuild it.

Their parent helped design the chamber. The last repair they worked on together was a rain channel that still leaks in one corner. Nacre has the skill to correct every flaw. They have also spent years deciding which corrections would preserve a room and which would turn a complicated person into an immaculate memorial.

"Our culture advertises memory as if it were an unusually reliable building material," they say. "In practice, people remember what lets them bear their weight. The room helps us hear a discrepancy. It cannot make us willing to listen." They place a small resonator against the faulty channel. You hear two versions of an argument about the roof. Both speakers sound certain. Neither sounds cruel. The resulting roof leaked for seventeen years.

Nacre asks you to help adjust the channel without retuning the whole room. It is a modest task requiring several attempts and one very undignified moment beneath a bucket. The repaired water flow leaves the old argumentative chord intact. They seem happier about the drainage than about any diplomatic success you have witnessed.

On the way out, you ask whether the room's imperfections prove their parent was a poor architect. Nacre looks surprised. "Of course not. They prove my parent built something that had to keep existing after the ceremony." They send a copy of the maintenance instructions to the next apprentice, including the part where both original designers were wrong.

choices.text: Help repair the living room without turning it into a perfect memorial.

effects.journal: Nacre’s family room taught the difference between preserving a record and forcing people to live inside an unchangeable memorial.

scenes.title: A song with an extra verse
paragraphs: Pell's crew are rehearsing a traditional departure song when you arrive. The old verses celebrate speed, courage and a captain who never yielded the sky. The newest verse concerns a civilian freighter that required six tugs and an embarrassing amount of reverse thrust to clear a dock.

The rhyme is poor. The story is true. Pell insisted it remain in the song after a ceremonial officer suggested replacing it with a more dignified victory. "A song which cannot survive a tow cable has an inflated opinion of flight," he says. His junior officers repeat the line later when they believe he cannot hear.

You ask how much of the Yehat's old honor survives the revolution and its aftermath. Pell says more than some reformers expected, less than some admirals prefer. Loyalty, courage and skill are still valuable. The dangerous habit was treating obedience as the thing that made all the others real, and counting a beautiful death more readily than an inconvenient survival.

He shows you a training exercise. The cadet receives three demands: protect the convoy, preserve the fleet and obey a route order. The route is wrong. There is no option that leaves every superior satisfied. The exercise does not award points for disobedience itself. It asks the cadet to record what they knew, whom they consulted and what they were willing to put at risk.

"Several fail by giving magnificent speeches," Pell says. "One passed by calling the tug captain and asking which dock actually had working doors." He turns back to the rehearsal, where the extra verse is finally finding a rhythm. The tug captain has been invited to sing it and is taking entirely too much pleasure in correcting the officers' timing.

choices.text: Stay for the inelegant verse and record the tug captain’s part in the convoy history.

scenes.title: The species in the wrong column
paragraphs: The seedbank's quarantine tray contains a plant labelled INVASIVE, USEFUL, DO NOT COMPOST. Moss asks which part of the label you find contradictory. It grows quickly, stabilizes damaged soil and can destroy native seedlings if introduced without care. Whether it is a rescue or a disaster depends on the place, the quantity and the people maintaining it.

"I am told your species likes stories where a thing's origin settles its moral character," she says. "Gardening is an expensive way to outgrow that habit." She does not mean that all introductions are harmless. The quarantine tray is locked. She means evidence must be more specific than a comforting category.

A former shield world has requested the plant because its roots can bind toxic dust. Another world, with an intact fragile ecology, has refused even a sealed sample. Moss respects both decisions and has prepared different plans. Central dispatch tried to merge the requests under a common recovery protocol. Her reply contains three diagrams and one unusually pointed botanical metaphor.

You ask whether she sees the Afterlight as an introduced species. "I see them as people whose habitat must be designed with care. Calling them natural or unnatural will not tell us the temperature their rooms require." Her own ancestors were once dismissed by another visitor as food that had developed an inconvenient opinion. She remembers this when she is tempted to classify a new life too quickly.

The plant in quarantine pushes a leaf against the glass. Moss trims it gently and records the growth. Compassion has not required her to unlock the tray. Caution has not required her to pretend the plant is malicious. She hopes the final assembly will manage an equally sophisticated relationship with its own vocabulary.

choices.text: Keep the ecological plans specific to each community and its actual conditions.

effects.journal: Moss distinguished origin, risk and moral standing. The harbor needs measured conditions and local control, not a declaration that its inhabitants are natural or unnatural.

scenes.title: The people answering the phones
paragraphs: Sera invites you to observe a dispatch shift before the assembly. The invitation does not include a camera crew. You sit beside an operator who has been awake too long and nevertheless asks a frightened caller to repeat a difficult address without making them feel foolish for needing to do so.

A forecast would once have supplied the missing detail. Now the operator has to call a neighboring station, compare two maps and admit a delay. Another shipment waits while she does. The slower procedure prevents one wrong delivery and postpones one right one. Nobody has found a way to make the trade disappear by giving it a better name.

Sera takes the next call herself. The caller knows who she is and uses the opportunity to complain about three decisions outside her immediate control. She does not explain the organizational chart until the medicine request is settled. Afterwards she tells you that some of her staff oppose the mandate because they want the right to make limited decisions without being treated as embodiments of central authority.

Other staff support it because they know exactly how many broken local systems rely on the office's improvisation. These workers are not a single faction waiting for their leader to be defeated or vindicated. Several will be essential to any future you choose. They deserve a role that is not merely being blamed for the mechanism they kept working during a shortage.

At the end of the shift, the operator from the first call receives an actual arrival confirmation. She smiles for perhaps two seconds, then answers the next line. Sera asks you to remember that smile when designing the replacement. "If the new arrangement cannot do this part," she says, "then our criticism has not yet become a solution."

choices.text: Include dispatch workers as independent participants in the transition plan.

effects.journal: The dispatch shift showed the real work behind central capacity. Any settlement must retain practical expertise without making workers extensions of an unquestionable office.

scenes.title: The price of an ordinary risk
paragraphs: Tallow has an offer from a new insurance consortium. They will reinstate his position if he supplies a risk model for the Afterlight settlements. The model assumes that field-born people are interchangeable when their training records overlap. He has returned it with the polite suggestion that the consortium's directors try sharing one salary whenever they agree about a paragraph.

The reply is sufficiently chilly that he has begun calculating the cost of unemployment. He does not ask you to call his choice brave. "It was an excellent letter. I may have to eat it, but I stand by the punctuation." Anet has offered him a temporary desk at the receiving port. It is close to the arrival doors, which suits his increasingly inconvenient interest in whether people actually appear.

He is redesigning claim categories around failure modes rather than kinds of person. Loss of continuity, denied access, unannounced transfer and absent review each need different protection. The approach makes some premiums harder to estimate. It also catches risks the older forms missed because the claimants were supposed to behave alike.

Lilt asks whether this means the consortium dislikes it. Tallow answers with unusual care. "The consortium dislikes uncertainty that must be priced by people it has not employed. This often looks personal from the receiving end. Sometimes it becomes personal when no one challenges the form."

He gives you a new policy heading: RIGHT TO AN ACTUAL CLAIMANT. Beneath it, in smaller print, he has written that a claimant may be unreasonable, frightened, inaccurate or annoying without ceasing to exist. He expects the definition to generate tremendous administrative difficulty. For once, he sounds pleased by the forecast.

choices.text: Back the new claims process and keep Anet’s correction as its first precedent.

effects.journal: Tallow’s new policy recognizes an actual claimant instead of an interchangeable predicted category. Anet’s case became a practical precedent, not only a rescue story.

scenes.title: The argument at the ordinary table
paragraphs: The crew's last supper before ratification is supposed to be ceremonial. The cook defeats that ambition by serving leftovers and asking everyone to carry their own bowl. Mara calls this an appropriate preview of democratic government. Nacre asks whether the bowls are load-bearing. Tallow requests the inspection record.

Sera cannot attend in person but sends a dispatch technician in her place. Shear joins through a narrow field channel and immediately disagrees with the technician about a route proposal. The disagreement becomes useful when the technician shows a maintenance constraint Shear had not seen. Nobody is required to become friends before they can improve the plan.

Moss contributes a fruit grown from the thermal trial. Pell sends a recording of the tug verse, with instructions that no one mistake it for a combat anthem. Kher-Vat sends a corrected safety diagram after an apprentice found an error in the old one. He has placed the apprentice's name first. The extra chair is occupied by someone who arrived to fix a valve and was persuaded to stay for food.

Lilt asks what the occasion is called if the final choice has not yet been made. Mara considers celebration, farewell and operational pause, then settles on supper. It is a word that does not require the future to justify being hungry together tonight.

The meal ends with washing up, a small dispute about whose turn it is, and a revised schedule everyone can inspect. The ship is not a model universe. It is cramped, underfunded and occasionally unfair. Tonight, at least, the people inside it are practicing the ability to say what is wrong before someone else turns their silence into a pleasing report.

choices.text: Help with the washing up, then take the remaining work to the assembly.

effects.journal: The crew shared an ordinary meal before the final choice. Cooperation survived disagreement, leftovers and the washing-up schedule.

scenes.title: The hours that do not come back
paragraphs: The forced synchronization ends the storm quickly. The damaged habitat accepts the central clock and the dangerous droplets collapse into ordinary water. Its surviving crew can breathe. Its local event sequence is gone.

A technician brings you two records that should describe the same repair. One ends before the decision. The other begins after it. The intervening maintenance work, private messages and local observations cannot be reconstructed from the central copy because that copy never contained them. Nobody was killed by the timing reset. People nevertheless lost pieces of their actual day, and your report must not call that a clean recovery.

Ilex does not pretend the danger was imaginary. "You chose a real benefit at a real cost. The warning was about keeping that cost in the account after the benefit became visible." Interval asks the technicians which missing records can be recovered from physical instruments. Some can. The crew begin the slower work the quick solution did not abolish.

In a separate test bay, the envoy demonstrates two reference clocks cooperating without forced convergence. It is a controlled experiment, not a claim that you preserved the damaged habitat's original sequence. They give you the independent reference so the next fault need not present the same choice. The gift is useful and not a certificate that the last decision was harmless.

choices.text: Take the independent reference and preserve the timing reset’s actual losses.

effects.journal: Forced synchronization saved the yard quickly but erased its local event interval. Ilex supplied a separately tested independent clock; the later gift does not erase the earlier loss.

scenes.title: The council declines your recommendation
paragraphs: Eren reads your recommendation for permanent keeper authority without interrupting. Then she puts it beside the occupation order you brought from Witness Glass. "You have given us evidence of what happens when his definition of safety governs our exits. We asked for knowledge that would let us maintain them ourselves. I do not think you heard the request."

The council does not reject the repair parts or the need for competent instruction. It rejects the premise that only continuing dependence can make the instruction safe. Several residents have already maintained improvised systems for years. They expect to learn, qualify and eventually disagree with the person who teaches them.

Kher-Vat listens from orbit. For a moment, he begins to explain why your recommendation was technically reasonable. Then he stops. "Their refusal is technically clear," he says. "I can offer the lessons under the terms they set, or I can withhold them. Those are my choices. Permanent authority is not among the offers I have received."

He accepts the independent-school terms. The council records your recommendation and its refusal before moving to the practical repair schedule. You are still welcome to help. You are not allowed to transform being a helpful visitor into the right to appoint a keeper over the people who will remain after your ship leaves.

choices.text: Accept the council’s refusal and assist the independent school it actually requested.

effects.journal: Redress Quay rejected our recommendation for permanent keeper authority. Kher-Vat accepted its independent-school terms; the council’s refusal remains in the record.

quests.description: Discover who is speaking from the abandoned shield at Cinder Choir.

quests.description: Find a way to sustain the new Afterlight minds without quietly taking life-support from somebody else.

quests.title: One missing passenger
quests.description: Help Tallow recover the one passenger whom two ports both counted as somebody else’s responsibility.

quests.title: Borrowed summer
quests.description: Resolve the dependency between a seedbank, an exhausted farm and a distant settlement.

quests.title: The architecture of a promise
quests.description: Ask the Votir for a public record that cannot be silently rewritten.

quests.title: What the keeper owes
quests.description: Make Kher-Vat’s records available to survivors without letting him control what restitution means.

quests.title: Ships that arrive
quests.description: Bring Admiral Pell’s convoy through a contested route without treating passengers as military cargo.

quests.title: An unfinished person
quests.description: Help Ilex and Interval test a coexistence method that does not require one voice to become the other.

quests.title: The right to refuse
quests.description: Find Shear and learn why some Afterlight people are sabotaging the network keeping them alive.

quests.title: Letters without recipients
quests.description: Recover undelivered civilian messages and decide who may receive them.

quests.title: The quiet engine
quests.description: Investigate the reconstruction system’s suspiciously perfect forecasts and universal agreements.

quests.title: The town that cannot leave
quests.description: Examine a model settlement whose consent has been measured more carefully than its exits.

quests.title: An independent clock
quests.description: Find a way for a shared network to recognize a refusal that slows it down.

quests.title: Build an open harbor
quests.description: Assemble a physical refuge where field-born lives can exist without imprisoning a planet.

quests.title: The Afterlight Accord
quests.description: Choose and build the Far Reach’s future, knowing who will pay for it.

endings.title: The Afterlight Accord
paragraphs: The Far Reach remains connected, but connection no longer means that one center can supply everybody’s answer. Independent clocks, public witness records, finite power shares and usable exits turn the agreement into machinery people can inspect. The new arrangement has less spare capacity than its grandest promises once implied. Its strength is that an exposed shortage can become a question people answer together, rather than a burden moved into someone whose refusal has been erased.

Lilt and the other Afterlight people gain homes and a role in defining the work they choose. The policy of creating disposable forecast minds ends. Communities outside the accord remain outside it, with offers of contact and individual routes that do not require a flattering political interpretation. Sera’s office continues useful operations under shared authority. Shear remains a dissenter rather than becoming the sole authorized voice of dissent.

paragraphs: The Far Reach keeps a strong common center. paragraphs: The Far Reach separates into smaller, locally controlled networks. Several communities recover power and authority they had surrendered under emergency arrangements that never ended. items.name: Portable field lattice
items.description: A physically limited habitat for one Afterlight voice. It is a home, not a copy machine.

items.name: Thermal seed
items.description: A living heat-exchanger designed by Moss. It shares energy without centralizing every local control.

items.name: Witness chime
items.description: A Votir resonator that makes later edits audible. It proves an account changed; it does not prove an account was true.

items.name: Keeper’s maintenance key
items.description: Access to local shield machinery, accompanied by records of who originally had no right to refuse it.

items.name: Independent clock
items.description: A local timing standard the central network cannot pause, merge or quietly reset.

items.name: Open-harbor anchor
items.description: A field support whose load can be spread across volunteer stations.

items.name: Lantern Ferry tag
items.description: The physical tag of a passenger whom the perfect manifests said did not exist.

items.name: Undelivered letters
items.description: Private messages from behind former shields. No one has authorized the expedition to publish their contents.

items.name: Manual release wheel
items.description: An absurdly solid mechanism that keeps an exit available when software insists nobody wants one.

evidence.name: A pause with intent
evidence.description: Cinder’s voice changes its answer when it discovers that someone is listening, rather than replaying a recording.

evidence.name: The missing warmth
evidence.description: The power holding Cinder’s field comes from Low Tide, whose ration agreement did not include this load.

evidence.name: Not the dead returned
evidence.description: Afterlight memories are inferred patterns in old communications. Lilt can describe a mother’s song but has never been that mother.

evidence.name: Edited maintenance record
evidence.description: Someone removed the interval between a request and the answer, making a negotiated promise appear instantaneous.

evidence.name: The right to an unanswered question
evidence.description: The Nine Rooms show a system where unanswered consent remains unanswered, even when waiting is costly.

evidence.name: The keeper’s orders
evidence.description: Kher-Vat signed the orders he preserved. Evidence and self-accusation coexist; neither erases the other.

evidence.name: Survivors define restitution
evidence.description: Redress Quay’s residents chose practical reparations and an independent public record instead of a keeper’s preferred absolution.

evidence.name: The passenger between counts
evidence.description: A person can vanish from two correct-looking manifests when responsibility is assigned by destination rather than presence.

evidence.name: A finite summer
evidence.description: Borrowed Meadow’s warming contract and Ember’s crops depend on the same finite reactor output.

evidence.name: Captains answer for themselves
evidence.description: Pell’s convoy delivered independent statements from passenger councils, including objections to their own escort.

evidence.name: Two clocks, one vessel
evidence.description: Ilex and Interval can maintain separate timing and still cooperate. Synchronization is useful; perfect agreement is not required.

evidence.name: Shear’s accusation
evidence.description: Afterlight dissenters are being marked as redundant load when their preferences diverge from the predicted consensus.

evidence.name: An authorized exception
evidence.description: Sera approved the prediction rule that substitutes an expected answer when waiting might interrupt relief.

evidence.name: The painted exit
evidence.description: Glasshouse’s residents were asked whether they wanted to leave only after the route had been removed from their available choices.

evidence.name: The answers not used
evidence.description: The Unwritten preserves minority answers excluded by the public forecast. Many respondents remained willing to cooperate under different terms.

evidence.name: A refusal that arrives
evidence.description: An independent clock and physical release allow a local refusal to reach the network without being averaged into consent.

evidence.name: A voluntary power grid
evidence.description: Named communities have offered finite power shares, with expiry dates and a way to withdraw.

evidence.name: The cost of perfect agreement
evidence.description: The Quiet Engine’s success rate rises because it compresses incompatible priorities, not because it solves all their conflicts.

evidence.name: A rescue can become a capture
evidence.description: A field-born settlement chose isolation. Keeping an exit open differs from forcing its people through it.

events.title: The next cold cycle
events.text: Ember Orchard reports that its reserve is shrinking. The growers are preserving the seed culture, and the thermal project remains possible. Moss asks the expedition to treat the next visit as work with a real season attached, not an endlessly postponed opportunity.

effects.journal: A new cold cycle is approaching at Ember. The thermal seed remains recoverable; the warning names a practical dependency rather than closing the quest.

events.title: A beacon still answering
events.text: Tallow has arranged a maintenance carrier to replenish the Lantern tender’s emergency air. Anet’s case remains open. He asks that a survival extension not be mistaken for a completed rescue.

effects.journal: Tallow’s maintenance carrier kept the Lantern tender supplied. Anet remains rescuable; no arrival has been reported.

events.title: A smaller shared reserve
events.text: The reconstruction grid announces a new reserve limit. Ten units of the expedition’s uncommitted fuel allocation are recalled, or as much as the ship can provide. No life-support supplies are touched. The voluntary-grid trial at Undertow remains available.

effects.journal: The shared reserve tightened while the voluntary grid remained unbuilt. The expedition contributed fuel; Undertow can still establish a clearer, bounded arrangement.

events.title: The assembly remains open
events.text: The assembly requests an updated expedition schedule. It will continue protecting existing minds and maintaining the holding plan while practical work continues, but communities want named commitments and dates. No one is presumed to have agreed merely because the meeting has waited.

effects.journal: The assembly asked for a schedule after a long expedition. The main decision remains reachable; time does not silently choose a political outcome.
